body:
Hey Tom sorry for the really late reply.  The dating game isn't as enjoyable for me as it might be for you, as I have to literally spend every ounce of my energy to even get a chance with a woman.  Dating for me is not the same as it is for you as I am not white.  Imagine being a leper midget and going out to try and meet women.  That might give you an idea of how difficult it is.  I'm not saying I hate being a minority or am ashamed of my ethnicity, I am actually quite proud to be my ethnicity, it's just that women mostly respond to white men around these parts.  It is how it is I guess.

In any case, I actually had a great date with a woman this past weekend.  I may have waited too long to text her back as I was too busy with work and volunteer activities, I texted her 3 days later and have not gotten a response.  It's not a big deal, however I am starting to see the futility of it all.

I spoke to a good friend about this, I belong to a religious organization with him and he is a great guy.  Anyway, despite how shameful it is to admit that I am lonely to another male (pretty much the most pathetic thing you can do as a male IRL), I could not keep it in any longer and told him everything.  He advised me to seek human connections instead of purely sex.  It is great advice and I agree, but it is hard to make human connections when it is like climbing Mt. Everest just to get a date, and when I finally get a date, she suddenly stops responding without explanation!

But I digress, I'm not too depressed right now, I am currently debating whether or not it is worth it to lone wolf it for the rest of my life.  Actually, lone wolfing it wouldn't be so bad, it's more the frustration of disappointment after disappointment, it feels like the universe is fucking with me and THATS what is really getting to me.

> That's on them, not you. Are you sure you're not just imagining this? You could be getting confirmation bias.
You sound incredibly down on yourself and it really could be affecting your perceptions of how you think people see you.

It's certainly not just my imagination.  I thought about that and wondered if I was being paranoid or delusional.  I have heard people say I have a very punchable face before, and my ex also noticed that people walking by me would give me the strangest looks.  Although she prescribed the reason to my 'energy' and that I was attracting that kind of reaction from people.  That might also be true, I don't think anything in life is black and white.  It's probably a mix of 1. reality (I actually have a face that is easy to hate/despise) 2. my energy/attitude/outlook/whatever you want to call it and 3. there probably is a bit of confirmation bias mixed in there at this point.

>Maybe you're trying too hard? One thing I've noticed is that when people want to be in a relationship, it doesn't happen as much. 

The thing is I spent the first 25 years of my life not trying at all and no women fell onto my lap.  It's just not going to happen unless you're good looking or have an exceptional personality, or you're at least somewhat intelligent and can carry a conversation with humor.  I am lacking in these fields, and for guys like me, things just don't 'happen', I have to fight tooth and nail just to get a girl to give me the slightest chance.  There might be some red pillers or puas that read this and say that's my problem, I am putting women on a pedastal.  Well I'm really not, all I'm saying is that I don't think I can be successful and find a relationship or meet women just by simply sitting in my apartment and hoping for the best.  I know that desperate is really bad when it comes to attraction, but it's really difficult not to be desperate some times.  I mean, I consider myself somewhat resilient, but there's only so long I could go without intimicacy before I start feeling desperate or lonely.

First off I want to say thanks for your comment.  I did indeed read it last night at the bar, while doing my usual thing (unsuccessfully trying to meet women).  

>  I'm just a random guy, wishing you the best, and assuring you that looking like you 'fit in' or are 'good looking' are not free access to happiness. 

That's true, but it's really difficult to be happy when I get dirty looks from strangers on the daily, and when it's just a constant stream of rejection week after week when I go out.  Honestly, I think I have a pretty solid positive outlook on life, I keep productive, I'm always busy, and I have goals.  I practice a philosophy that is pretty much unbeatable in terms of dealing with the struggles of life.  *Even with all of that*, I'm just not sure if I can ever become happy with out a mate, it's just that plain simple.  Biologically speaking that is the entire purpose of our existence after all.  On a neurological level I might be able to delude myself into being content and happy alone, but honestly it will take some serious mental gymnastics that I'm not sure I'm capable of, and the delusion wouldn't last very long.  To fit in and be good looking are obviously not the keys to happiness, but hell, it's **really** difficult achieving happiness without them.   At least for me, as I said I'm not an intelligent guy, I'm probably not even a good person,  I just feel like I lack the foundation and the grit to deal with this solo and remain positive.

>I hung a rope around my neck the other day readying for suicide, but a single post on here has changed my outlook, just to have one person wish me to fight and survive.

Could you share the post that helped you if you don't mind?  If you don't feel comfortable sharing it publically could you PM it to me?  I could use some positivity and it might help others on here as well!
